1. Executive Overview

American Express (AXP) has delivered extraordinary long-term returns for shareholders over the past five decades. From an adjusted closing price of $1.22 on June 01, 1972, the stock reached $305.99 by March 11, 2026, representing a cumulative total return of 24,895% and a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.81% over 53.8 years.

The stock's all-time high of $384.04 was recorded on December 11, 2025, while the adjusted all-time low of $0.38 dates to October 03, 1974. Despite severe drawdowns — most notably during the 2008 Global Financial Crisis — AXP has consistently recovered and reached new highs, underscoring the resilience of its franchise.

Key Takeaway: A long-term buy-and-hold position in AXP has been handsomely rewarded, with the stock compounding at approximately 10.8% annually. However, investors have endured peak-to-trough losses as deep as -83.9%, requiring conviction during periods of extreme market stress.
